# LANventory

> Inventory system for LAN parties: assets with inventory number, category, name and serial
> number, configurable fields per category, and tracking of DGUV V3 electrical inspections
> (German focus). One Go binary, SQLite, server-rendered web UI.

Key concepts (details in docs/concepts.md):
- Asset: one physical item (single assets only, no quantity items). Has an inventory number,
  category, name, serial number, location, status and the custom fields of its category.
- Inventory number: generated from `inventory.number_format` (default `{prefix}-{seq:05}`, for
  example `SL-00042`; the prefix comes from the category and is optional; `{seq:04}` gives plain
  numbers 0001, 0002, … shared by all categories); can be overridden manually; unique.
- Category: defines the (optional) number prefix, the DGUV settings and custom fields. Field types: text,
  number, select, bool, date. Number fields can have a unit (for example `m`). Editable in the
  web UI by admins; German templates (power strip, cable drum, ...) are seeded once. The
  category of an existing asset can be changed (values move by field key, the number and the
  inspections stay); a category with assets cannot be deleted.
- Asset list (`/assets`): search, filters by category, location, status and the select/bool
  fields of a category, sorting, paging; the state is in the URL query. Each asset has a change
  history built from the audit log.
- Location: a flat list (no hierarchy), for example "Storage 1". Cannot be deleted while assets
  use it.
- Asset status: active, defective, retired, lost.
- DGUV V3 inspection: periodic test of portable electrical equipment. A category can require it
  (`dguv_required`) and sets the interval in months; an asset can override the interval. An
  inspection is a record (no editing; admins can delete): date, inspector name (may be an
  external electrician), result (pass/fail), protection class, visual and functional check,
  reason (initial, repeat, repair), measurements (protective conductor resistance in ohm,
  insulation resistance in megohm, protective conductor / leakage current in mA with its method
  direct, differential or alternative, touch current in mA; a reading beyond the instrument's
  range carries a qualifier `<` or `>`, for example `>299`), test device with ID and calibration
  date, remark, the applied interval and the next due date
  (inspection date plus interval in calendar months, clamped to the month end). Only users with
  the `can_inspect` flag record inspections; only assets of DGUV categories that are not retired
  or lost can be inspected. A failed inspection can set the asset to defective. LANventory shows
  non-binding hints for values outside simplified limits of DIN VDE 0701-0702 but never decides
  pass or fail. LANventory documents inspections; it does not replace a qualified electrician.
- Inspection pages: `/inspections/due` (overdue, due within 30 days, never inspected; filters
  category, location, state), `/inspections` (list with filters date range, result, category,
  location, inspector; CSV export at `/inspections.csv` with the same filters), `/inspections/{id}`
  and the printable protocol `/inspections/{id}/print`. The dashboard shows the counts.
- CSV: `/assets.csv` exports the asset list (same filters and sort, up to 50 000 rows; columns
  inventory_no, category, category_prefix, name, serial_no, manufacturer, model, location, status,
  purchase_date, dguv_interval_months, note, last_inspected_on, next_due, then `field:<key>` per
  custom field; UTF-8, comma, CRLF; cells starting with `=+-@` get a leading apostrophe).
  Editors and admins import CSV files at `/assets/import` (upload up to 5 MB, delimiter and
  encoding auto-detected incl. Windows-1252, column mapping, preview, one transaction, all or
  nothing or skip invalid rows, existing inventory numbers skipped or updated). The export
  can be imported again unchanged. Optional inspection columns (inspected_on, inspector_name,
  result, reason, protection_class, visual_ok, function_ok, pe_resistance_ohm, insulation_mohm,
  leakage_ma, leakage_method, touch_ma, test_device, test_device_id, test_device_calibrated_until,
  remark; German headers and values such as bestanden, SK I, `>299` are recognized) record a past
  inspection per row for DGUV categories (identical inspections are not duplicated; only users with
  `can_inspect`; a failed result does not change the status). There is no CSV API.
- Bulk edit: editors and admins tick assets in the list (or "all matches of the filter", at most 1000) and
  change category, location, status, manufacturer, model, purchase date, DGUV interval, note and custom
  fields at once (custom fields when the assets end up in one category); preview (dry run), then one
  transaction, all or nothing; name, serial number and inventory number are not bulk-editable. API: `PATCH /api/v1/assets`.
- Data export/import: admins download the whole inventory including inspections as one JSON file
  (`GET /admin/data/export.json`, format `lanventory-export`, version 1: locations, categories
  with fields, assets with field values and inspections; no users, tokens or settings) and import
  it at `/admin/data` or with `lanventory data import` (preview, one transaction, existing
  inventory numbers skipped or abort, dry run). It moves data between instances; there is no API for it.
- Roles: viewer < editor < admin (viewers read, editors change assets and locations, admins
  manage categories and users). The flag `can_inspect` (right to record inspections) is
  independent of the role.
- Login: password plus optional second factor (TOTP app, passkey, single-use recovery code), or
  passwordless with a passkey. Admins can require a second factor for admins or everyone.

Units and conventions: timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC in the API (Unix seconds in the database);
lengths and other measures are numbers, the unit comes from the field definition.

## API (v1)

JSON under `/api/v1/`; the OpenAPI 3.1 spec is the single source of truth.
- [OpenAPI spec (JSON)](/api/openapi.json) (also `/api/openapi.yaml`)
- [API docs](/api/) (human-readable, generated from the spec)

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer lvk_...` (tokens are created by users in the web UI under Account >
API tokens, shown once, stored hashed). A token acts as its owner with at most the owner's current
rights; effective permission = scope AND role. Scopes: `read:assets` (locations, categories,
assets), `write:assets` (create/update/delete assets and locations; deleting an asset needs an
admin owner; categories are read-only), `read:inspections`, `write:inspections` (needs the owner's
`can_inspect`; deleting an inspection needs an admin owner). A logged-in browser session works too
(header `X-CSRF-Token` on unsafe methods). Per-token rate limit (HTTP 429).

Conventions: snake_case JSON, timestamps RFC 3339 UTC, dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, numbers as numbers;
custom field values in `fields` ({key: value}: number, boolean or string by field type). Lists:
`?page=&per_page=` (max 200) and `{items, page, per_page, total}`. Errors: RFC 9457
`application/problem+json` with stable `code` (not_found, invalid_token, insufficient_scope,
forbidden, validation_failed with an `errors` map per field, conflict, rate_limited, csrf_failed,
...). PATCH is partial. Inspections cannot be edited.

Endpoints:
- `GET /api/v1/me`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/locations`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/v1/locations/{id}` (409 while in use)
- `GET /api/v1/categories`, `GET /api/v1/categories/{id}` (fields: key, label, type, unit, options, required)
- `GET|POST /api/v1/assets` (filters q, category, location, status, f_<key>; inventory_no optional on create),
  `GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/v1/assets/{id}` (category immutable), `GET /api/v1/assets/by-number/{inventory_no}`
- `PATCH /api/v1/assets` (bulk): body `{"ids": [1,2], "changes": {...}, "dry_run": false}` applies the same
  change (category_id, location_id, status, manufacturer, model, purchase_date, dguv_interval_months, note,
  note_append, fields) to up to 1000 assets, all or nothing; name, serial_no, inventory_no are not allowed;
  422 errors are keyed "<asset id>.<field>"
- `GET /api/v1/inspections` (from, to, result, category, location, asset, inspector),
  `GET|DELETE /api/v1/inspections/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/inspections/due` (state, category, location),
  `GET|POST /api/v1/assets/{id}/inspections`

Examples:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://inventory.example/api/v1/assets?q=drum&status=active"
    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://inventory.example/api/v1/assets/by-number/KT-00012
    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"category_id": 2, "name": "Drum 25 m", "fields": {"length": 25}}' https://inventory.example/api/v1/assets
    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"result": "pass", "visual_ok": true, "function_ok": true, "insulation_mohm": ">299"}' https://inventory.example/api/v1/assets/12/inspections

Full guide: docs/api.md (in llms-full.txt together with the OpenAPI spec).
